LESSON: PHONIC AWARENESS (F-J)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Reading 2.1 Visual discrimination (5 lessons) By the end of the sub strand the l
Topic 2.2: Phonic awareness (f-j)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Phonic awareness (f-j), part of Reading 2.1 Visual discrimination (5 lessons) By the end of the sub strand the l in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why are there different sounds in the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Phonic awareness (f-j) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving is enhanced as the learner objectively matches letter sounds with corresponding objects

with the same sound for easy memorization.

Values:
● Responsibility is developed as the learner independently matches letter sounds with corresponding objects.

● Love is developed as the learner chants with others letter sounds in harmony and without conflicts.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Effective communication as a life skill is enhanced as the learner chants rhymes on letter sounds.

● Child safety and security is enhanced as the learner becomes more aware of the immediate environment and what to do and

not to be safe.

Link to other Learning Areas: Mathematics as learners count the first phonic sounds

Suggested learning resources: Letter flash card, box, bag or basket to hold the letter cards
